caption:
In 2017 Google changed its ad auction formula and prices went up about 15%.

That is Michael Whinston, the MIT economist testifying for the Department of Justice, before Judge Amit Mehta.

The mechanism: Google gave the second-place bidder a built-in handicap so their offer came in closer to the winner's. That closed the gap between what the winner paid and what the winner was actually willing to pay. The gap was yours. Now it is not.

Nothing about your account changed that year. Your costs did.

This is the whole argument against letting one channel carry all your lead flow, however well it is performing right now. A channel you do not control can reprice you overnight, and you will spend a quarter blaming your creative.

Source: Whinston testimony, US v. Google, October 2023.
